title: One-day scent trail
intro: Indian garlands, Malay-Muslim attar, colonial spices and Teochew incense, in one walkable day through Little India, Kampong Gelam, Fort Canning and Chinatown. Press play to walk it on the map, or open the whole route in Google Maps.
tip: Shop and workshop hours change, so check before you go. Sifr Aromatics workshops need booking.

stops.name: Kopi at Tekka Centre
stops.blurb: Start like a local: kopi or teh at the hawker drinks stalls, with Indian breakfasts all around you.

stops.name: Jothi Store & Flower Shop
stops.why: Garlands strung fresh for the Serangoon Road temples, since the early 1960s.
stops.blurb: Jasmine, rose and marigold garlands hang across the shopfront. NHB lists it as a Little India heritage business.

stops.name: Jamal Kazura Aromatics
stops.why: Singapore's oldest homegrown perfume business, selling attar since 1933.
stops.blurb: Alcohol-free minyak attar in rows of glass bottles, a few steps from Sultan Mosque. The shop is one of NHB's Street Corner Heritage Galleries.

stops.name: Lunch by Sultan Mosque
stops.blurb: Nasi padang, murtabak or Turkish grills around Bussorah St and North Bridge Rd.

stops.name: Sifr Aromatics
stops.why: Blend your own perfume with a third-generation Kazura perfumer.
stops.blurb: Johari Kazura, grandson of Jamal Kazura's founder, opened Sifr in 2010. Book the workshop ahead.

stops.name: Fort Canning Spice Garden
stops.address: Canning Rise, Fort Canning Park, Singapore
stops.why: Crush a clove leaf where Raffles planted Singapore's first spice garden. Free.
stops.blurb: Nutmeg, clove, pepper and torch ginger on the site of the 1822 First Botanic Garden, with a free Spice Gallery in the underpass.

stops.name: Wak Hai Cheng Bio
stops.why: Giant spiral incense coils smoking over the courtyard of a national monument.
stops.blurb: Teochew settlers built a shrine to Mazu here in 1826, when the sea still came up to Philip Street.

stops.name: Dinner at Maxwell Food Centre
stops.blurb: End at a hawker centre, with a squeeze of calamansi on your plate.
